explanation: Daily scanner runs, staffed threat-intelligence and disclosure intake, scheduled testing, and manual control reviews identify technical and process weaknesses.
additionalAssurance: A daily reconciliation checks that every detection source reaches our tracking register.

explanation: Analysts maintain a daily reviewed register covering ownership, evaluation, exploitation evidence, mitigation, remediation, and reporting for every detected vulnerability.
Missed scans, review failures, and reporting errors become vulnerability tickets with owners and tracked corrective actions.
Microsegmentation, restricted administration, and hardened templates contain compromise and keep recovery procedures manageable.
Legacy scans run automatically, but costly workflow integration leaves evaluation and response tracking manual.
customerRisk: Manual handoffs can delay action on agency-impacting findings.
providerCompensation: Supervisors reconcile scan results and tickets daily.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can review the weekly exception summary and escalate missing actions.

explanation: Legacy deployment tooling lacks automatic detection after changes because integrating representative tests is complex.
customerRisk: Changed resources may expose agencies before the next scheduled scan.
providerCompensation: Operators manually scan changed resources before release and verify isolation.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request the release test record before enabling affected integrations.

explanation: Credentialed scans use dedicated restricted identities without disabling endpoint protection, firewall controls, or production hardening.
A release checklist compares images against the current KEV catalog and blocks activation until listed vulnerabilities are removed.
We scan every resource and do not exercise the optional sampling permission.
Process owners verify and validate all non-machine resources quarterly and record completed reviews in the register.
Machine scanning meets the fourteen-day Class C interval, but some legacy configuration and process drift checks remain monthly.
customerRisk: Undetected drift can expose agency workloads between reviews.
providerCompensation: Change approval and microsegmentation reduce unreviewed changes and lateral movement.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can limit integrations and request configuration evidence for important changes.

explanation: Stable machine resources receive monthly scans, but some stable non-machine resources receive only quarterly detection reviews.
customerRisk: Stale procedures or configuration assumptions could persist beyond the Class C monthly target.
providerCompensation: Owners review operational exceptions weekly and investigate reported inconsistencies.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can flag unexpected behavior and request focused reviews.

explanation: We meet the highest-risk Class C impact-reduction intervals but cannot consistently meet every lower-risk interval on tightly coupled legacy components.
completionTargetExplanation: Supplier-dependent upgrades prevent a reliable completion estimate.
customerRisk: Some agency exposures may persist beyond recommended intervals.
providerCompensation: Isolation and targeted filtering reduce exposure while owners track remaining risk.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can restrict affected integrations until verified risk reductions are reported.

explanation: Maintenance meetings assign remaining vulnerabilities for mitigation or remediation based on recorded residual risk.
The response lead checks the KEV catalog daily and schedules actual remediation by its due dates even when interim mitigations are effective.
Legacy scanners cover daily high-risk samples, but some isolated machine groups are sampled weekly rather than every three days.
customerRisk: Vulnerabilities in those groups may remain undetected longer than recommended.
providerCompensation: Strict ingress rules and daily host alerts help identify suspicious activity.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can keep connections to those groups disabled unless needed.

explanation: This offering uses Rev5 Class C, so 20x machine verification does not apply; we address VDR-TFR-MVF.
Administrators verify and validate all machine resources monthly using configuration exports, health checks, and documented manual review.
Analysts manually evaluate exploitation prerequisites against actual system configuration and document the supporting evidence for each finding.
Analysts trace direct and indirect internet payload paths, including application-mediated paths across microsegmented networks.
The response lead assigns N0–N5 ratings using likely effects on each agency and shared-service impacts, retaining the rationale and history.
The evaluation checklist assumes automated exploitation unless documented technical evidence proves otherwise.
We track findings individually because reliable grouping across inconsistent legacy inventories would require costly integration.
completionTargetExplanation: Individual tracking will remain our approach for the current platform.
customerRisk: Duplicate records can increase workload and delay related responses.
providerCompensation: A coordinator reconciles affected components daily and assigns shared owners.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request a consolidated explanation for findings affecting the same service.

explanation: Analysts inspect affected versions and reproduce findings where safe before documenting false positives.
Manual assessments cover criticality, reachability, exploitability, and privilege, but documentation of the other contextual factors remains inconsistent.
customerRisk: Missing prevalence or vulnerability-interaction evidence may understate agency impact.
providerCompensation: Senior analysts review high-impact decisions and known threat intelligence daily.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can provide mission context and ask for reassessment of disputed ratings.

explanation: A daily reconciliation produces controlled updates for all necessary parties covering all new activity, including manual verification and validation.
Analysts populate all applicable VER-RPT-VDT fields, including times, historical ratings, reduction plans, overdue explanations, and disposition, then validate the exported JSON.
A separate register supplies all required accepted-vulnerability fields, including acceptance reasons and practical agency mitigation information.
The reporting lead removes exploit-enabling details while providing necessary parties enough evidence for risk-based decisions.
Reports summarize scanning and patching, but consolidating penetration tests and disclosure activity into an overview remains manual and incomplete.
customerRisk: Agencies may underestimate activity outside routine scanning.
providerCompensation: Detailed underlying records remain available through controlled sharing.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request the separate testing and disclosure summaries.

explanation: We exercise the public-disclosure permission only after the security lead determines publication is unlikely to enable exploitation.
All necessary parties receive a consistent human-readable report every month, assembled and checked by two analysts.
The response lead marks a vulnerability accepted immediately when remediation or full mitigation within 192 days is unlikely and reviews elapsed time daily.
Reports are shared securely, but automated retrieval of historical JSON is unavailable because the legacy reporting platform lacks a suitable interface.
customerRisk: Agency systems cannot automatically reconcile recent historical activity.
providerCompensation: We supply manually exported historical records on request.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can reconcile those exports against monthly reports.

explanation: Daily triage handles urgent findings, but some routine evaluations take seven days rather than the Class C five-day target.
customerRisk: Delayed contextual evaluation may postpone agency risk decisions.
providerCompensation: The duty analyst escalates suspected high-impact exposures immediately.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can flag critical dependencies for expedited evaluation.

explanation: Incident procedures cover confirmed exploitation, but qualifying internet-reachable likely exploitable findings do not consistently enter incident handling before exploitation.
customerRisk: Agencies may receive incident-level coordination later than recommended.
providerCompensation: The duty lead sends urgent risk notices and isolates affected components.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can trigger their own incident review when notified of these exposures.

explanation: For the Class C optional incident classification, we escalate non-internet-reachable likely exploitable N5 findings until verified reduction to N4 or below.
